messages:
leah: Posting a customer repro. They see scrambled words after an auth refresh during streaming. Happens with python-sdk sampleapp.
leah: Repro (flaky): start long gen -> simulate token refresh (client reconnect ~150ms) -> reconnect with resume token header -> final output has older chunk appearing after newer ones.
omar: Which resume mechanism? Python SDK uses resume_token header by default unless browser.
leah: Correct. We also support Last-Event-ID fallback but customer is on python-sample which sets resume param.
omar: Can you paste the raw SSE frames captured by tcpdump? Need to check event boundaries and ordering.
leah: Wire trace (trimmed):
```
: ping
event: message
id: 512
data: {"seq":512,"part":1,"text":"Inte"}

connection: reset

: ping
event: message
id: 513
data: {"seq":513,"part":1,"text":"rnal "}
event: message
id: 512
data: {"seq":512,"part":2,"text":"rface"}
```
leah: Client assembled: "Inte rnal rface" instead of "Internal Interface". Basically part 2 of 512 arrived after seq 513 started.
omar: That matches a proxy behavior where buffered outgoing fragments are flushed asynchronously on disconnect, so replayed fragments can interleave with newly-generated fragments on resume.
python-bot: QC noted: STREAM-PY-47 created for flaky repro.
omar: Short-term mitigation: add a defensive reassembly in python-sdk that groups by (seq, part) and holds emission until either all parts for a seq are seen or a small timeout expires (e.g., 80ms) when reconnecting. Will open a micro PR.
leah: That should reduce user-visible scrambling. Do ensure the timeout is tunable and opt-in so we don't increase latency for normal streams.
omar: Agreed. Longer-term: runtime/proxy should surface an explicit X-Chunk-Seq and X-Chunk-Part header and avoid mixing replayed fragments with live fragments by draining the proxy queue before starting resumed replay. Posting to eng-runtime. @eng-runtime any thoughts?
eng-runtime: We can add a drain-before-resume toggle. Also adding X-Chunk-Seq header is easy. But need to coordinate with SDKs for rollout; we'll gate the change behind a feature flag for ~2 weeks.
leah: Nice. I'll coordinate with customer to try a canary.
ci-bot: deploy: sampleapp/python-sdk/0.4.9 -> canary at 2026-04-02T08:12:00Z by omar :rocket:
omar: PR up: https://git.internal/r/python-sdk/201 (adds buffering + flaky test harness simulating auth-flap). Tests include deterministic flappy-proxy emulation.
leah: Thanks. Once canary verifies, let's document behavior in docs/streaming-reconnects.md and include guidance on tuning the sdk buffer timeout.
eng-runtime: Will file runtime ticket PROXY-1402 to add drain flag and X-Chunk-Seq support. We'll also add a small compatibility note for Last-Event-ID consumers.
leah: Leaving this thread open until canary result and PROXY ticket assigned.
